verses.text: At that time Herod, the ruler of Galilee, heard the reports about Jesus.
He said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has come back from the dead! That is why he has the power to do miracles."
Herod had arrested John, tied him up and put him in prison. He did this because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
John had been telling Herod, "It is against the law for you to have her as your wife."
Herod wanted to kill John, but he was afraid of the people, because they believed John was a prophet.
On Herod's birthday the daughter of Herodias danced for the guests, and Herod was very pleased with her.
So he promised with an oath to give her anything she asked for.
Her mother told her what to say. So she said, "Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a plate."
The king was very sad. But he had made a promise in front of his guests, so he ordered that her request be granted.
He had John's head cut off in the prison.
John's head was brought in on a plate and given to the girl, and she took it to her mother.
John's followers came and took his body and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard what had happened, he left in a boat and went by himself to a quiet place. But the crowds heard about it, and they followed him on foot from the towns.
When Jesus came ashore, he saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them and healed those who were ill.
When evening came, his followers came to him and said, "This is a lonely place, and it is already getting late. Send the crowds away, so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food."
Jesus replied, "They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat."
They answered, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish here."
"Bring them here to me," he said.

Then he told the people to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven and gave thanks. Then he broke the loaves and gave them to his followers, and the followers gave them to the people.
They all ate and had enough. Then the followers picked up twelve baskets full of the pieces that were left over.
About five thousand men ate, as well as women and children.
Straight away Jesus made his followers get into the boat and go on ahead of him to the other side of the lake, while he sent the crowd away.
After he had sent them away, he went up on a mountainside by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.
By this time the boat was far out on the lake. It was being battered by the waves, because the wind was blowing against it.
Shortly before dawn, Jesus came out to them, walking on the lake.
When the followers saw him walking on the water, they were terrified. "It's a ghost!" they said, and they cried out in fear.
But straight away Jesus spoke to them. He said, "Cheer up! It is I. Do not be afraid."
"Lord, if it is you," Peter replied, "tell me to come to you on the water."
"Come," Jesus said. So Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water towards Jesus.
But when he saw how strong the wind was, he was afraid and began to sink. He cried out, "Lord, save me!"
Straight away Jesus reached out his hand and caught him. "Your faith is so small!" he said. "Why did you doubt?"
When they climbed back into the boat, the wind stopped.
Then those in the boat worshipped Jesus and said, "You really are the Son of God!"
After they had crossed the lake, they landed at Gennesaret.
When the people there recognised Jesus, they sent the news all around that area. People brought to him everyone who was ill.
They begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes, and all who touched it were healed.
